claims.claim: A small minority of checking accounts pay the great majority of overdraft fees, while most accountholders pay none in a given year
A typical overdraft fee is about thirty-five dollars
High-to-low transaction reordering was standard practice at the largest US banks
In 2010, federal judge William Alsup in San Francisco found Wells Fargo had reordered debit-card transactions high to low and ordered it to return $203 million to California customers
Banks argued in litigation that high-to-low ordering reflected customer preference for large items such as rent and car payments clearing first
Overdraft fees generated billions of dollars a year in US bank revenue
A 2010 rule required banks to obtain customer opt-in before charging overdraft fees on debit-card transactions
Capital One eliminated overdraft fees in 2021, and Ally did so the same year
